thread.title: Federal Government Rules Out Immediate Electricity Tariff Increase
thread.title_full: Federal Government Rules Out Immediate Electricity Tariff Increase

author: LeadershipNGA
title: Federal Government Rules Out Immediate Electricity Tariff Increase
text:
The Federal Government says it has no immediate plans to raise electricity tariffs, while prioritising service improvements, reliable power and universal metering. The position was restated at the inauguration of a 3MW captive solar hybrid project at Yakubu Gowon University in Abuja.
The Federal Government has reiterated that it has no immediate plans to increase electricity tariffs, assuring Nigerians that its priority is to improve service delivery, expand access to reliable electricity and accelerate universal metering across the country.
Minister of Power Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe made the clarification while speaking with the media at the inauguration of a three megawatts captive solar hybrid power project at the University of Abuja, now known as Yakubu Gowon University. There are no immediate plans to increase electricity tariffs. Our goal is to build a commercially viable power sector while protecting vulnerable consumers, Tegbe said. The minister said the administration was focused on addressing the structural and financial challenges confronting the electricity sector.
He added that improvements in supply must be matched by greater efficiency and accountability across the value chain. Tegbe said universal metering remained a major priority for the ministry and the wider reform programme. He explained that expanded metering would promote more accurate billing, improve transparency and ensure consumers are charged according to measured electricity consumption. The government's clarification comes amid renewed political interpretation of the minister's earlier comment about the possible removal of electricity subsidies.
It also follows concerns that the government could introduce another tariff adjustment. Tegbe stressed that tariff increases were not an immediate consideration. Instead, the government is concentrating on improving service delivery, strengthening consumer confidence and expanding access to dependable electricity. The administration is continuing to examine reforms to the electricity subsidy framework as part of efforts to address the sector's longstanding financial challenges.
However, the government has maintained that any such reforms must take the needs of vulnerable consumers into account. The broader objective, according to the minister, is to establish a financially sustainable and investment-friendly electricity market. Such a market would support infrastructure development, improve generation and distribution, and deliver more reliable power to households, businesses and public institutions. The inaugurated project is designed to provide stable and cleaner electricity to a university community of approximately 58,726 students.
It is expected to significantly reduce the institution's reliance on diesel-powered generators. The Rural Electrification Agency developed the project under Phase II of the Energising Education Programme. Its infrastructure comprises a 3.3MWp solar array, 3MW AC output and a 2MWh battery storage system. The solar facility is supported by dedicated grid supply outside solar generation hours.
This arrangement is intended to help maintain electricity availability when solar generation is unavailable or insufficient to meet demand. The project also includes the installation of 388 solar-powered streetlights across the university campus. The lighting is expected to improve visibility and security while creating a safer environment for students and staff to study and move around after dark. According to Tegbe, the inauguration highlights the Federal Government's broader commitment to improving the quality and reliability of electricity supply.
It also reflects the administration's pursuit of reforms designed to strengthen the power sector's long-term sustainability. The project forms part of wider efforts to improve electricity access at public institutions and reduce dependence on expensive fossil-fuel generators. Its hybrid design combines renewable generation, battery storage and grid support to provide a more dependable supply. The government said its reform agenda would continue to address financial pressures and structural weaknesses across the electricity value chain.
It aims to create conditions that encourage investment while improving performance for consumers. For now, the government's position is that there will be no immediate increase in electricity tariffs. Its stated focus remains service improvement, nationwide metering, consumer protection and the development of a commercially viable and sustainable power sector.
